title: Who Do Perspectivist Models Predict Well? Annotator Agreement, Sparsity, and Performance
abstract: arXiv:2610.22567v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Successful completion of perspectivist natural language processing (NLP) annotation tasks requires algorithms to be aligned across diverse perspectives in order to predict how different humans will rate text. This work studies how the performance of such algorithms varies for annotators who behave differently than others, either by providing annotations that diverge from others' responses or by providing fewer annotations altogether. To aid with characterizing model performance, we curate the largest collection to date of perspectivist NLP datasets with ordinal annotations. After evaluating multiple classes of perspectivist algorithms across each of the datasets, we model the relationship between individual annotator idiosyncrasy and algorithm performance. translated_title: 视角主义模型对谁预测得好？标注者一致性、稀疏性与性能
translated_abstract: 成功完成视角主义自然语言处理（NLP）标注任务，需要算法在不同视角之间保持对齐，以预测不同人类将如何对文本进行评分。这项工作研究了此类算法的性能在那些行为与他人不同的标注者上如何变化——这些标注者要么提供与他人回答相分歧的标注，要么提供的标注总量较少。为了帮助刻画模型性能，我们整理了迄今为止规模最大的带有序数标注的视角主义NLP数据集集合。在各个数据集上评估了多类视角主义算法之后，我们对个体标注者的独特性与算法性能之间的关系进行了建模。总体而言，我们发现算法在倾向于与他人保持一致的标注者上表现更好，但标注者的响应率与算法性能之间并不存在统计学上显著的正相关。
tldr: 该研究通过构建迄今最大的序数标注视角主义NLP数据集集合，发现算法对倾向于与他人一致的标注者预测效果更好，而标注者标注量的多少与算法性能并无显著正相关。
en_tdlr: By curating the largest collection to date of perspectivist NLP datasets with ordinal annotations, this study finds that perspectivist algorithms predict better for annotators who tend to agree with others, while annotator response rate shows no statistically significant positive correlation with algorithm performance.
